title: Beyond Liu's 0.382709 threshold for the union-closed sets conjecture
summary: The union-closed sets conjecture asks whether every finite union-closed family containing a nonempty set has an element contained in at least half of its members. Let $c_{\mathrm{UC}}$ denote the largest universal lower bound on this proportion. The best previously proved lower bound is due to Liu and is above $0.3823455$; his own numerical optimization suggested a stronger threshold $c_{\mathrm L}>0.382709087918735$.
